title: Recorded test results
lead: Representative results show which settings and playback operations were checked, with their media, environment and measurement units. They are records of specific runs, not guarantees for every source or device.

blocks.text: These rows summarize separate checks documented for each app. Their media and workloads differ; do not add the case counts or durations into one suite. The Web row identifies the measured source revision and ordinary patched measurements.

blocks.text: Native API and lifecycle checks recorded on 2026-10-22

These records cover the added configuration editors, API operations and owner replacement. Each row identifies its source and environment. The separate configuration, playback, GUI and build checks are reported individually; their case counts are not added together. Main source labels identify the corresponding app-specific source files. Their equality check does not establish that shared packages, generated assets or native app binaries match the recorded build. The labels do not indicate a post-merge test run.

blocks.text: Read CPU and memory values in context

Web CPU times are totals across the measured workload, not CPU utilization percentages. Renderer-process CPU excludes the separate browser and GPU processes. The heap values are ordinary samples whose size depends on collection timing; one MiB is 1,048,576 bytes. JavaScript heap is not total player memory: decoded frames, native media buffers and GPU allocations are outside it.

The Web runs ended with seven Players created and destroyed, no live Player or media element, no pending media request, and the app metrics timer stopped. This short desktop workload does not establish long-session memory behavior, leak freedom or performance on other hardware. The recorded numbers are not pass/fail budgets.
Build checks and real playback are different evidence

Type checks, builds and unit tests with mocked players check code and configuration contracts. Real SDK playback checks also require advancing native time and visible video or subtitle cues for the named action. Applied bitrate/buffer getter values show that settings reached the SDK; they do not measure bandwidth enforcement or buffering performance.

Simulator/emulator results do not qualify physical devices, every UI factory, protected media, casting or Analytics receipt. Browser automation can check a collector request attempt without establishing remote collection or dashboard aggregation. Check the platform chapters and SDK references for the operation you want to try.
